title: Approach to Anemias: Microcytic, Macrocytic and Hemolytic
summary: A structured workup of anemia using indices, reticulocyte count and key confirmatory tests.
objectives: Use the reticulocyte index to separate underproduction from destruction/loss.
Recognize the lab pattern of hemolytic anemia.
Distinguish iron deficiency from thalassemia trait.

highYield: Low reticulocyte production index (< 2) = underproduction; high (> 2) = loss or hemolysis.
Hemolysis labs: low haptoglobin, high LDH, high indirect bilirubin, positive urine hemoglobin.
Iron deficiency: low ferritin, high TIBC, low iron; thalassemia trait: normal/high ferritin, normal RDW.
quickReview.mnemonic: Hemolysis: Low haptoglobin, LDH up, indirect bili up.

deepStudy.introduction: Anemia is a sign, not a diagnosis. The first branch point is the reticulocyte production index (RPI), which corrects the reticulocyte count for the degree of anemia and maturation time.

sections.heading: Underproduction anemias
sections.body: Microcytic: iron deficiency (most common worldwide), thalassemia trait, anemia of chronic disease (often normocytic), sideroblastic anemia. Macrocytic: B12/folate deficiency (megaloblastic with hypersegmented neutrophils), liver disease, hypothyroidism, myelodysplasia.

sections.heading: Hemolytic anemias
sections.body: Intravascular hemolysis destroys cells in the vessel (e.g., PNH, mechanical valves, ABO incompatibility): hemoglobinemia, hemoglobinuria, low haptoglobin. Extravascular hemolysis (e.g., hereditary spherocytosis, warm AIHA) occurs in the spleen with splenomegaly.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: Missing hemolysis delays treatment of life-threatening causes (TTP/HUS, transfusion reactions). Missing B12 deficiency can cause irreversible neurologic damage.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: Ferritin is an acute-phase reactant — it can be falsely normal in inflammation; interpret with CRP/ESR.
examTraps: A normal ferritin does not exclude iron deficiency during infection or inflammation.
Reticulocyte count must be corrected (RPI) — an uncorrected count in severe anemia is misleading.

memoryHooks.text: Iron studies: TIBC high + ferritin low = iron deficiency (storehouse empty, transport busy).
memoryHooks.funny: Bantay: 'Ferritin = bodega ng bakal. Pag zero na ang bodega, kahit mag-deliver pa si TIBC, kulang pa rin.'
